title: Hello, Aether
theory:
Every Aether program starts at main(). println writes a line to standard output.

String interpolation uses ${...}, so println("n = ${n}") prints the value of n. Press Run to compile and execute this on the Aether server.

title: Functions & loops
theory:
Functions annotate their return type with -> T. Parameters are typed; everything else is inferred.

The loop for i in 1..5 counts 1 through 4, the upper bound is exclusive. Change the range and Run again.

title: Actors
theory:
An actor owns private state and handles typed messages in its receive block. No shared memory, no locks.

Send a message with !. Each Inc updates the count and prints it, so this run shows the state building up across two messages.

title: Error handling
theory:
Functions that can fail return a (value, error) tuple. Check the error first, an empty string means success. No exceptions, no hidden control flow.

Discard an error you don't need with _. This is the same convention the standard library uses everywhere.

title: Pattern matching
theory:
Aether has Erlang-style pattern matching. Write a function as several clauses that match on argument values, with optional when guards.

It replaces long if/else chains with declarative, readable dispatch. The first matching clause wins.
starter_code:
factorial(0) -> 1
factorial(n) when n > 0 -> n * factorial(n - 1)

classify(x) when x < 0 -> "negative"
classify(x) when x == 0 -> "zero"
classify(x) when x > 0 -> "positive"

main() {
    println("5! = ${factorial(5)}")
    println("classify(-3) = ${classify(-3)}")
    println("classify(7)  = ${classify(7)}")
}

title: C interop
theory:
Aether compiles to C, so it calls C directly. extern declares a C function; libc is always linked, so no extra setup is needed here.

This is how Aether reaches any C library: declare the signature, call it like a normal function. See C Interoperability.
